chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

My father used to say: 'Whoever performs Tawaf around this House (the Kaaba) for seven circuits, and prays two Rak'ahs on whichever side of the Masjid he desires, Allah will write for him six thousand good deeds, erase from him six thousand sins, raise for him six thousand levels, and fulfill for him six thousand needs. So whatever of these is hastened, it is by the Mercy of Allah, and whatever is delayed, it is out of Desire to listen to his supplication.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for performing Tawaf and two Rak'ahs of prayer at the Kaaba?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the specific numerical rewards of six thousand for each spiritual benefit highlight the immense virtue of combining circumambulation with prayer, a practice emphasized in Shia jurisprudence as a means of comprehensive spiritual purification. The distinction between hastened rewards through divine mercy and delayed ones due to longing for supplication reflects the Shia theological understanding of God's responsiveness to the believer's persistent engagement and emotional connection during worship.
